name: Sintered Rare-Earth (NdFeB) Permanent Magnets: India's REPM Scheme Award
scope: India's Rs 7,280 cr sintered NdFeB magnet scheme (REPM): the 20-bid tender awaiting award, listed bidders and would-be magnet makers, upstream feedstock names and magnet-importing customers.

summary.one_line: MHI holds 20 bids for five REPM slots (6,000 MTPA, Rs 7,280 cr) with awards still pending; listed small/mid-cap exposure is thinner and murkier than 'rare earth stocks' lists imply - 20 Microns is a confirmed bidder, the Midwest bid sits in promoter-group entities rather than listed Midwest Ltd, and Sona Comstar is not on the reported bidder list.
key_points: Cabinet approved the REPM scheme on 26 Nov 2025: Rs 7,280 cr outlay (Rs 6,450 cr sales-linked incentives over five years plus Rs 750 cr capital subsidy) for 6,000 MTPA of integrated capacity split among five beneficiaries of up to 1,200 MTPA each (S2).

MHI received 20 bids on the CPP portal by 12 Aug 2026 and opened technical bids on 13 Aug 2026 (S1); the tender is a two-stage Least Cost System, so financial-bid opening and selection come next, and no award has been reported as of this edition (S5, S3).

Listed bidders named in the MHI list: Coal India, L&T, 20 Microns and Starteck Finance (an RBI-registered NBFC); the Midwest bid is a JV of Midwest Energy Ltd and Midwest Advanced Materials, promoter-group entities rather than the listed granite company Midwest Ltd (S3, S8, S23).
Unlisted or foreign heavyweights are in the race: NEO Performance Materials (Singapore), Proterial India, Lohum, Attero and ReNew (S3).

Exposure is acute: India imported 53,748 t of magnets in FY25 per government data (S16), China makes about 90% of the world's rare earth magnets (S9), and the April 2025 Chinese licensing regime cut Bajaj Auto's Chetak output to 10,824 units in Jul 2025 from 20,384 a year earlier (S17).

Feedstock is the binding constraint: 6,000 t of magnets needs about 1,500 t of rare earth oxide versus about 500 t IREL can supply (S11); IREL's NdPr oxide capacity is 400 MTPA, with 500 MTPA of IREL supply earmarked for the first three beneficiaries (S6).
China's October 2025 controls are only suspended until 10 Nov 2026, while the April 2025 licensing on Dy/Tb and other elements remains in force (S19).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Any listed REPM winner gets up to 1,200 MTPA of subsidised capacity backed by a share of Rs 6,450 cr in five-year sales-linked incentives (S2) - most material for a small cap like 20 Microns, a confirmed bidder (S3).

Permanent Magnets Ltd's wholly owned subsidiary Quantum Magnetics won MeitY ECMS approval to make neodymium magnets on 18 Aug 2026, a parallel localisation route that does not depend on the REPM award (S12).
Motor and EV component makers such as Sona Comstar, which imported 120 t of magnets from China in a year (S9), would gain a domestic second source if localisation succeeds.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Several of the five slots could go to unlisted or foreign bidders (NEO, Proterial, Lohum, Attero, ReNew), leaving little direct listed exposure (S3).
Early Indian magnets are expected to cost 20-25% more than Chinese imports (S7); Sona Comstar's MD has asked for testing infrastructure to assure domestic REPM quality (S11).
Oxide shortfall: of about 1,500 t of oxide needed, about 1,000 t must be sourced outside IREL (S11).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: MHI financial-bid opening and award of the five REPM slots after the 13 Aug 2026 technical-bid opening (S1, S5).
Commissioning of Midwest Advanced Materials' 500 t/yr Hyderabad plant (S7) and Quantum Magnetics' Phase 2 capex scheduled for Q3FY27 (S12).
China's decision on the suspended October 2025 controls before 10 Nov 2026 (S19).

subsections.title: What sintered NdFeB magnets are and why they matter

blocks.text: Sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) rare earth permanent magnets are among the strongest permanent magnets and are vital for electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics, aerospace and defence (S2). The REPM tender covers the integrated chain - oxide to metal, metal to alloy, and alloy to finished magnet (S14) - which is much harder than final machining alone.

India imported 53,748 t of magnets in FY25 per government data (S16); the figure covers all magnet types, not only NdFeB. China produces around 90% of the world's rare earth magnets (S9). The Mines Minister has said India's REPM consumption is expected to double by 2030 (S15).

China's April 2025 controls on seven rare earths, including Dy, Tb and Sm, require MOFCOM export licences and remain in force; the broader October 2025 controls, including extraterritorial rules, are suspended only until 10 Nov 2026 (S19).

The 2025 shock was real: Bajaj Auto made 10,824 Chetak e-scooters in Jul 2025 versus 20,384 a year earlier (S17). Sona Comstar restored motor volumes by July 2025 by switching sub-10-15 kW designs to light-rare-earth magnets without Dy/Tb (S10).
Sona Comstar puts India's heavy-rare-earth magnet imports at about 3,600 t a year, of which about 1,200 t go to autos (S10) - so the 6,000 MTPA scheme target is large relative to current auto demand.

blocks.text: Sona Comstar said in 2025 it planned to make magnets locally (S9), but it does not appear in the reported REPM bidder list (S3).

items: 20 Microns: confirmed REPM bidder (S1, S3). We found no public disclosure of capacity, capex or technology partner, so execution credibility cannot yet be assessed.

Midwest Ltd: listed Black Galaxy granite producer. The NdFeB plant belongs to Midwest Advanced Materials (MAM), a promoter-group company named in the DRHP (S8), not a subsidiary. MAM's 500 t/yr Hyderabad plant has a Rs 250.86 cr project cost with Rs 125 cr government support, uses NFTDC technology, and targets 5,000 t/yr by Dec 2027 (S7).

Permanent Magnets Ltd: magnet and current-sensing component maker whose wholly owned subsidiary Quantum Magnetics received ECMS approval for neodymium magnets; Phase 2 capex (block cutting, machining, surface treatment) is due in Q3FY27 (S12). It is not on the REPM bidder list (S3).
Starteck Finance: NBFC listed as a bidder (S3, S23) with no disclosed magnet assets.

blocks.text: Governance check on Midwest Ltd: the REPM bid and magnet plant sit in promoter-group entities (S3, S8); listed shareholders have no stated economic claim on them unless that changes.

items: Rare Earth Exchanges: L&T's partner search exposes the core bottleneck - commercial magnet-making know-how; about 25 companies attended the April pre-bid meeting (S14).
Rare Earth Exchanges: Midwest Advanced Materials' early magnets are expected to cost 20-25% more than Chinese imports, with NdPr and Dy/Tb sourcing a strategic vulnerability (S7).
Saur Energy: the bidder mix spans PSUs, renewable IPPs, engineering firms and specialist magnet players, signalling changing competition (S4).
Rare Earth Exchanges on Hindustan Zinc: no resource estimate has been disclosed for its REE block, and India still lacks separation and magnet capability (S18).

blocks.text: The theme is partly discovered: brokers and media framed Coal India and L&T as stocks 'in focus' on the bid news (S20), and Sona Comstar's magnet plans have been covered since 2025 (S9). Coverage of 20 Microns and Starteck as bidders is largely limited to reproductions of the bidder list (S3, S20). Permanent Magnets Ltd rose 3.5% on the ECMS approval day but was only about 5.9% higher over six months (S12).
numbers.json was not present in this folder, so this edition does not tabulate 3/6/12-month returns or attribute price moves to rare earth news beyond what cited sources state.

items: Award mix: foreign or unlisted bidders (NEO, Proterial, Lohum, Attero, ReNew) may take most of the five slots (S3).
Feedstock: the roughly 1,000 t oxide shortfall beyond IREL must be imported (S11), while the April 2025 Chinese licensing regime still covers Dy/Tb (S19).

Cost and quality: early domestic magnets are expected at a 20-25% cost premium (S7) and OEMs want testing infrastructure (S11); Sona Comstar has shown it can design around heavy rare earths (S10), which could cap demand for premium grades.
Delays: the bid deadline already slipped from 28 May to 12 Aug 2026 (S5, S1).

companies.name: 20 Microns Ltd
companies.role: Small-cap named as a bidder in MHI's REPM tender (S1, S3).
companies.impact: A 600-1,200 MTPA slot (S6) would be transformative relative to its size; no capacity, capex or technology partner has been disclosed, so the award is a binary catalyst (S3).

companies.name: Midwest Ltd
companies.role: Listed Black Galaxy granite producer; promoter-group firm Midwest Advanced Materials builds the NdFeB plant and bid with Midwest Energy (S3, S8).
companies.impact: Magnet upside currently sits outside the listed entity; MAM's plant costs Rs 250.86 cr with a 5,000 t/yr ambition (S7) - watch for any transfer or related-party structure.

companies.name: Permanent Magnets Ltd
companies.role: Magnet and current-sensing component maker; wholly owned subsidiary Quantum Magnetics has ECMS approval for neodymium magnets (S12).
companies.impact: Localisation via ECMS rather than REPM; Phase 2 machining and finishing capex due Q3FY27 (S12).

companies.name: Starteck Finance Ltd
companies.role: RBI-registered NBFC (S23) named as a REPM bidder (S3).
companies.impact: No public magnet assets or partner disclosed; magnet link unclear (S3, S23).

companies.name: Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar)
companies.role: India's largest rare earth magnet importer: 120 t from China in a year, planned 200 t (S9).
companies.impact: Not on the reported REPM bidder list (S3); hedged with light-RE and magnetless motors (S10); benefits from domestic supply if quality is assured (S11).

companies.name: Bajaj Auto Ltd
companies.role: EV two-wheeler maker and magnet consumer (S17).
companies.impact: Chetak output fell to 10,824 units in Jul 2025 from 20,384 amid China curbs, so localisation reduces supply risk (S17).

companies.name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd
companies.role: REPM bidder; partnered with EVR Motors on EV traction motors (S3, S13).
companies.impact: Magnets support its motor plan but need a technology partner and are a small line item for the group (S13, S14).

companies.name: Coal India Ltd
companies.role: PSU REPM bidder setting up critical-minerals units in Chile and Singapore (S3, S22).
companies.impact: Diversification option; small relative to coal (S22).

companies.name: Gujarat Mineral Development Corp
companies.role: Developing the Ambadungar REE deposit; MoU with NMDC on an integrated rare earth value chain (S21).
companies.impact: Potential non-Chinese oxide source for magnet makers; commercial timelines unproven (S21).

companies.name: Hindustan Zinc Ltd
companies.role: Holds a 210 ha REE composite licence in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh (S18).
companies.impact: Exploration only; no resource estimate disclosed (S18).

method: First edition, researched 2026-10-03/04 with WebSearch and WebFetch. Scheme terms come from PIB, newsonair and trade-press reports of MHI notices; the bidder list is from the MHI release as reported by PSU Watch and Saur Energy. Company links were checked against filings and prospectus references (Midwest DRHP group companies; Permanent Magnets' 18 Aug 2026 ECMS disclosure). Several primary pages (PIB, BSE PDFs, Business Standard) returned 403 errors and are cited from search-result content where the facts were corroborated elsewhere. numbers.json was not present, so share-price returns are not tabulated. No ratings or price targets.
